claim: SEMI P44 defines 'OASIS.MASK', a common mask data format based on OASIS that applies to the input data format for mask tools.

claim: SEMI P44 was first published in November 2005 (P44-1105); the current version is P44-1216, reapproved in January 2024.
evidence: "Revision History SEMI P44-1216 (Reapproved 0124) SEMI P44-1216 (technical revision) ... SEMI P44-1105 (first published)" (SEMI store, P44 page)
notes: SEMI revision codes are MMYY.

claim: SEMI P45 defines 'MALY', a common job deck data format for mask tools, and references SEMI P39 (OASIS) and P44 (OASIS.MASK).
evidence: "This Document defines the common job deck data format specifications for mask tools, namely 'MALY'. MALY specification applies to the input data format for mask tools. Referenced SEMI Standards ... SEMI P39 ... SEMI P44" (SEMI store, P45 abstract)

claim: SEMI P10 standardises the data structures of photomask orders so that mask customers can place orders automatically and mask shops can return mask results and qualification data automatically.

claim: The latest SEMI P10 revision (P10-1112) has Inactive status because the conditions to maintain Current status were not met, though SEMI says inactive standards remain valid for use.
evidence: "Revision: SEMI P10-1112 - Inactive ... This Standard ... has an Inactive Status because the conditions to maintain Current Status have not been met. Inactive Standards ... continue to be valid for use." (SEMI store, P10 page)

claim: SEMI P10 specifies only the transmitted file format (UTF-8, with an authorised XML implementation), not a database or programming language.
evidence: "This structure only defines the data format for the transmitted file. No particular database or programming language is specified ... except that an authorized implementation in Extensible Markup Language (XML) format will be posted ... The data file is to be transmitted as a UTF-8 file." (SEMI store, P10 abstract)

claim: SEMI P39 (OASIS) is designed primarily to carry hierarchical mask layout between EDA software, mask writing tools and mask inspection/repair tools, and is hardware- and software-independent.
evidence: "This format is designed primarily to encapsulate hierarchical mask layout for interchange between systems such as EDA software, mask writing tools, and mask inspection/repair tools. This format is designed to be both hardware- and software-independent." (SEMI store, P39 abstract)

claim: OASIS was defined by a working group of SEMI's Data Path Task Force formed in autumn 2001, drawing on International SEMATECH meetings on mask EDA issues.

claim: A commercial mask-data viewer (Nippon Control System neoEBV) lists support for GDSII, OASIS, OASIS.MASK, OASIS.CL (SEMI P49), MEBES, JEOL, VSB and other writer formats, each with its own job deck format (e.g. MALY for OASIS.MASK, JB for MEBES).
evidence: Table 'Displayable Pattern File Format': "OASIS.MASK | SEMI P44-1105, SEMI P44-0709 P44-1216 | Maly (SEMI P45-0306N, SEMI P45-1218)"; "MEBES | | JB, Extended MEBES Jobdeck"; "OASIS.CL (SEMI P49) | SEMI P49-0823"; "P10 | | semi p10-0706e" (Supported Formats page)

claim: Under 15 CFR 734.7, unclassified software or technology made available to the public without restrictions on further dissemination - including posting on publicly available internet sites - is 'published' and not subject to the EAR (with exceptions for certain encryption and firearm files).
evidence: "unclassified 'technology' or 'software' is 'published,' and is thus not 'technology' or 'software' subject to the EAR, when it has been made available to the public without restrictions upon its further dissemination such as ... (4) Public dissemination ... including posting on the Internet on sites available to the public" (15 CFR 734.7(a))

claim: Inference: an open PDK posted on GitHub under Apache 2.0 (SKY130, GF180MCU, IHP SG13G2) is likely 'published' under 15 CFR 734.7 and outside the EAR, whereas a leading-edge commercial PDK distributed only under NDA is not published and remains subject to export controls and deemed-export rules.
notes: Combines @c_734_7 with @c_sky_noexport, @c_gf180_lic, @c_ihp_lic and @c_ep_tsmc. Not a legal opinion; SkyWater states 'no export control restrictions' but BIS has not ruled publicly on PDKs.

claim: ChipFoundry, a US SKY130 shuttle service, requires designers to complete an export compliance form and says most SKY130 designs are EAR99, with encryption for confidentiality, very high-performance compute and fast data converters as possible exceptions; it places final classification responsibility on the customer as exporter of record.

claim: ChipFoundry's tape-out submission flow is: run a local precheck on the wrapper GDS, upload via SFTP (or HTTPS/GitHub fallback) with a SHA-256 hash recorded, submit for review, pull the tape-out report, then 'confirm' to lock the submission as Final for fabrication; the last submission before the deadline is used unless confirmed earlier.
evidence: "A hardened wrapper GDS that passes cf precheck"; "Mode A: Default SFTP push"; "cf push --submit"; "The last successful submission before the deadline is treated as your tapeout version unless you later lock with cf confirm."; "cf confirm # locks submission_state to Final for fabrication" (Tapeout Submission Process, 30 Dec 2025)
notes: Workflow: trigger=shuttle deadline; actor=designer, platform reviewer; input=GDS + user_defines.v; system=SFTP/S3 + platform; output=Final-state submission; exception=precheck failure or review notes -> re-push.
